title: Killer Whales Make a Wave to Wash a Seal Off the Ice

scenes.text: Killer whales make their own waves to hunt.
A seal rests on a floating chunk of ice, too high to grab.
So the pod lines up and swims at the ice together.
At the last second they dive, and the wave they make washes over the floe.
In one Antarctic hunt, scientists counted 11 waves in about 28 minutes.
The waves broke the ice apart and finally knocked the seal into the water.

description:
Killer whales make their own waves to hunt.
In Antarctica, pods swim at an ice floe together, dive at the last second, and wash a seal into the water. Scientists counted 11 waves in about 28 minutes in one hunt.
Is this the smartest hunting trick you have seen?
first_comment: No tools, just teamwork and a wave. What other animal hunts this cleverly?
